title: Columnwise quasi-isomorphism from nested cutoff quotients to smart windows
statement: Let $C$ be abelian [def-sp-abelian] and $K$ a first-quadrant bicomplex [def-sp-double-complex-total]. For integers $a\le b$, write $A$ and $B$ for the columnwise cutoffs at $a$ and $b$ of [lem-sp-double-complex-vertical-tower-maps], and $R$ for the columnwise reextension into which these cutoffs include. Let $f:A\to B$ satisfy $f\,\iota_b=\iota_a$. There exists a bicomplex morphism $q:\operatorname{coker}(f)\to W[a,b)(K)$, with the smart window of [def-sp-double-complex-vertical-window], such that $q^{p,\bullet}$ is a quasi-isomorphism of nonnegative cochain complexes for every horizontal index $p$. No totalization or homology-of-total conclusion is asserted.

source.place: Proof step 1 of the cutoff-cone comparison: quotient of nested smart cutoffs maps to the smart window, before totalization.

proof.text: The cutoff inclusions are monomorphisms in every degree, so the compatibility with them determines f columnwise. Compose the b-cutoff inclusion with the projection onto the smart lower truncation at a and apply the b-cutoff functor to that projection. The resulting map B->W[a,b)(K) annihilates A: A has no terms in degrees >=a and the lower truncation has no terms below a. The cokernel universal property therefore gives q. Naturality of the projections makes q commute with the horizontal differentials.

source.place: Proof step 1 of the cutoff-cone comparison: quotient of nested smart cutoffs maps to the smart window, before totalization.

proof.text: If a<b, in each extended column the quotient has im(d^(a-1)) in degree a-1. In degree a it has the original term when b>a+1, or its cycles when b=a+1. The map to the window is zero in degree a-1, the quotient by im(d^(a-1)) in degree a, and an isomorphism in higher degrees. It is degreewise epi. Its kernel is the two-term complex im(d^(a-1))->im(d^(a-1)) in degrees a-1,a, whose differential is the canonical image isomorphism. This kernel is contractible, so the short exact homology sequence makes q a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Proof step 1 of the cutoff-cone comparison: quotient of nested smart cutoffs maps to the smart window, before totalization.

proof.text: For a=b, monicity forces f to be the identity, and both quotient and smart window are zero. Original columns were extended from nonnegative degrees: if a=0 the boundary image in degree -1 is zero; if a<0 the comparison is an isomorphism on the retained terms. Thus restriction to N does not remove a nonzero half of the contractible kernel. If b<=0 both sides are zero. This verifies the assertion for all integer endpoints.
